content.content: Reef early. Establish crew roles, marks on lines, and a clear sequence for tack/clew, halyard, and reefing lines.

Call the reef before you must; slow the boat first
Ease halyard to marks; secure tack; tension clew; re‑tension halyard
Verify leech line, luff tension, and vang/traveler settings

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Reefing Strategy & Procedures'?

sideB.content: Reef early. Establish crew roles, marks on lines, and a clear sequence for tack/clew, halyard, and reefing lines.

content.content: Keep reef lines fair and labeled. Inspect reef tacks, clew cringles, ram’s horn/hooks, and blocks for chafe.

Mouse and whip line ends; color‑code reefs (1/2/3)
Check cheek blocks, exit plates, and clutch wear
Stow excess tail to prevent snags during drops

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Mainsail Reef Hardware & Lines'?

sideB.content: Keep reef lines fair and labeled. Inspect reef tacks, clew cringles, ram’s horn/hooks, and blocks for chafe.

content.content: Choose the right headsail/reef for conditions. Roller reef to draft aft; maintain UV cover and proper halyard tension.

Reef to a flat shape; over‑roll for smaller area if needed
Keep furling line on a clean single layer on drum
Use halyard restrainer to avoid halyard wrap

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Headsail Selection & Roller Reefing'?

sideB.content: Choose the right headsail/reef for conditions. Roller reef to draft aft; maintain UV cover and proper halyard tension.

content.content: Balance power and helm by managing draft depth/position and leech twist with sheet, traveler, vang, outhaul, and Cunningham.

Use telltales: inside/outside luff for headsail, leech telltales on main
Flatten in breeze; add depth in light air
Adjust traveler for angle, sheet/vang for twist

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Sail Trim Fundamentals (Draft/Twist)'?

sideB.content: Balance power and helm by managing draft depth/position and leech twist with sheet, traveler, vang, outhaul, and Cunningham.

content.content: Cunningham moves draft forward and opens the leech when tensioned. Relieve in light air.

Mark halyard and Cunningham reference settings
Ease before reefing; re‑set after hoist
Avoid over‑tension that creates vertical wrinkles

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Luff Tension & Cunningham Use'?

sideB.content: Cunningham moves draft forward and opens the leech when tensioned. Relieve in light air.

content.content: Outhaul flattens or deepens the lower main; critical for pointing and depower.

Tight for upwind/breeze; ease for power offwind
Check clew slug/shackle and boom sheaves
Record base, light, and heavy settings

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Foot Tension & Outhaul Control'?

sideB.content: Outhaul flattens or deepens the lower main; critical for pointing and depower.

content.content: Steer and trim together. Avoid over‑trim and maintain flow across both sails.

Feather in puffs; ease sheet/traveler preemptively
Watch slot: headsail lead and main twist coordination
If backwinding, ease main or move traveler down

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Preventing Luffing/Backwinding'?

sideB.content: Steer and trim together. Avoid over‑trim and maintain flow across both sails.

content.content: Control the boom and headsail downwind to avoid accidental gybes and collapse.

Rig a real preventer to bow/padeye, not lifelines
Wing‑on‑wing with whisker pole; top/foreguy secure
Ease vang for safe gybes; re‑set after turn

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Downwind Control: Preventers & Pole Work'?

sideB.content: Control the boom and headsail downwind to avoid accidental gybes and collapse.

content.content: Set, trim, and douse with a snuffer if available. Keep loads manageable for short‑handed crews.

Hoist at deep reach; bear away to fill
Trim tack and sheet to project luff
Practice douses: leeward, windward, or letterbox

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Asymmetric Spinnaker Basics'?

sideB.content: Set, trim, and douse with a snuffer if available. Keep loads manageable for short‑handed crews.

content.content: Storm jib/tri‑sail plans keep control when conditions exceed normal reefing.

Dedicated tracks/attachment points verified
Practice setting on a calm day
Secure unused sails and lazy jacks

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Storm Sails & Heavy Weather Options'?

sideB.content: Storm jib/tri‑sail plans keep control when conditions exceed normal reefing.

content.content: Plan safe, quick drops to reduce deck time and flogging risk.

Head to wind or deep offwind to depower as appropriate
Flake as you drop; control halyard speed
Secure sail with ties to prevent re‑hoist in gusts

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Dousing & Drop Techniques (Main/Headsail)'?

sideB.content: Plan safe, quick drops to reduce deck time and flogging risk.

content.content: Extend life with regular inspections, UV cover maintenance, and chafe patches.

Inspect leech/foot lines, batten pockets, and slides
Fresh‑water rinse salt; dry fully before stow
Repair small tears early to prevent propagation

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Sail Care, Chafe & UV Protection'?

sideB.content: Extend life with regular inspections, UV cover maintenance, and chafe patches.

content.content: Smooth hoists depend on low‑friction luff hardware and maintained batten cars.

Lubricate with sail‑safe dry lube
Inspect cars, shackles, and track fasteners
Replace cracked slugs before failure

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Slides, Slugs & Batten Car Systems'?

sideB.content: Smooth hoists depend on low‑friction luff hardware and maintained batten cars.

content.content: Lead controls twist/draft. Adjust for even luff telltales and proper sheeting angle.

Forward for power/closed leech; aft for twist/depwer
Lock pins fully; avoid moving cars under load
Mark common lead positions

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Headsail Lead Position & Cars'?

sideB.content: Lead controls twist/draft. Adjust for even luff telltales and proper sheeting angle.

content.content: A controlled stop using backed headsail and eased main; reduces motion and buys time.

Tack without releasing headsail; back it to windward
Traveler up, main eased; rudder slightly to windward
Balance trim until leeway and drift are steady

sideA.content: What are the key points of 'Heaving‑To with Sails'?

sideB.content: A controlled stop using backed headsail and eased main; reduces motion and buys time.
